Effect and Acceptability points match. But the paper says distribution with guidance and naloxone may reduce immediate risks of fatal overdose; discouraging visual checks and using only with someone holding naloxone may mitigate false negatives and complacency. Last sentence corrected.
results.corrected_extracted: Hypotheses without data: where fentanyl is wanted, a positive result may be sought or fail to deter use, particularly in withdrawal; strips give no amount; contaminated spoons may give positives; it is unclear whether a test that routinely shows non-fatal fentanyl will promote complacency; strips may not reach the people most at risk. The authors nonetheless support handing out strips with clear guidance on reading results, alongside low-threshold naloxone and within broader harm-reduction services, which they say may reduce the immediate risks of fatal overdose; discouraging visual checks for fentanyl and encouraging use only in the company of someone with naloxone may, they say, mitigate the risk of false negatives and/or complacency.
